US Republican Senator from South Carolina Lindsey Graham recently introduced the Coast Guard Personnel Equipment Act, which would require all US Coast Guard uniforms to be produced in the US. 
Under current law, all branches of the US Armed Forces—except the US Coast Guard—are barred from purchasing clothes, fabrics, fibres, yarns and other materials that are produced overseas.

title: Sustained reforms key to navigating uncertainty in Vietnam: World Bank
summary:
Vietnam’s economy has demonstrated notable resilience in an uncertain global environment, according to the World Bank. 
While headwinds are expected to temper the pace of expansion, it projects growth will moderate to a still-robust 6.8 per cent in 2026, following an 8-per cent expansion in 2025, it recently said. 
While Vietnam’s outlook remains solid, risks remain elevated in the near term.

title: Benzene market stable-to-soft amid cautious textile, fibre demand
summary:
Asian benzene prices stayed stable-to-soft in May 2026, easing 5–6 per cent from April highs as textile and synthetic fibre buyers kept procurement cautious. 
However, prices remained around 25 per cent above 2025 levels, supported by higher crude and naphtha costs, balanced supply, steady nylon-linked demand, and China-led regional market influence.

title: India’s textile ministry, ICRIER sign MoU for policy research
summary:
India’s Ministry of Textiles and Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations (ICRIER) have signed an MoU to support data-driven policymaking for the textile and apparel sector. 
The partnership will strengthen textile data systems and provide analytical research inputs to help formulate robust policies for a sector that plays a major role in India’s manufacturing, exports and employment

title: Bangladesh net FDI inflows up 39.36% in 2025
summary:
Bangladesh’s net FDI inflows increased by 39.36 per cent last year to $1,770.42 million compared with $1,270.39 million in 2024, the Bangladesh Bank said. 
The increase was driven primarily by higher reinvested earnings and intra-company loans. 
Reinvested earnings rose by 318.25 per cent, from $103.79 million in 2024 to $434.10 million in 2025, while intra-company loans rose by 25.68 per cent.

title: UNECE speeds UN/LOCODE issuance to boost Gulf supply chains
summary:
UNECE has issued 3 new UN/LOCODE entries and updated 10 existing entries in the UAE to strengthen Gulf supply chain resilience amid Strait of Hormuz disruptions. 
The move supports inland logistics hubs, dry ports, rail terminals and multimodal corridors linking Abu Dhabi, Sharjah and Dubai to alternative export routes via Fujairah and Djeddah.

title: India’s NITI Aayog to revise MCA for multi-modal logistics parks
summary:
India’s NITI Aayog is working with the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and National Highways Logistics Management Limited to revise the model concession agreement (MCA) for multi-modal logistics parks to strengthen the concession framework for the project’s effective implementation. 
The MCA is undergoing deliberations to enhance biddability, viability and bankability of such projects.

title: Polyester yarn prices ease as PTA weakens on limited demand
summary:
Polyester yarn prices eased modestly on May 14, 2026, as PTA weakened across key Asian benchmarks amid limited downstream demand. 
FOB China 21s and 32s yarn declined by around 0.7 per cent, while PTA fell in China, Southeast Asia and South Korea. 
MEG stayed stable, and India’s CIF PTA price remained unchanged, reflecting cautious procurement.

title: South India cotton yarn sees mixed trend, prices up in Tiruppur
summary:
Cotton yarn prices in south India showed a mixed trend, with Tiruppur prices rising ₹4–5 per kg on limited mill supply, stronger export demand, higher ICE cotton prices and the CCI’s auction price hike.
Mumbai yarn prices remained steady after last week’s surge, as weak fabric lifting and labour shortages continued to weigh on domestic demand and yarn consumption.

title: UK’s clothing exports dip 7.8% to $884 mn in January-March 2026
summary:
United Kingdom clothing exports declined 7.87 per cent year-on-year to £655 million in January–March 2026, while textile fabric and fibre exports also weakened, according to Office for National Statistics data.
The fall reflected subdued demand in key European markets, cost pressures, and geopolitical uncertainties, although fibre shipments showed slight sequential improvement from Q4 2025.

title: Nigeria Kwara Garment Factory, KWS Garment Production Village ink pact
summary:
Nigerian state-run Kwara Garment Factory has signed a pact agreement with KWS Garment Production Village, allowing the latter to manage and run the former. 
A minimum of 80 per cent of the factory’s production workforce will be women and indigenes of Kwara state. 
The management model has been carefully structured to protect the state’s investment while allowing private sector excellence to thrive.

title: UK’s clothing imports fall 3% in Q1, sharply lower than Q4 2025
summary:
UK’s clothing imports declined 3.04 per cent year-on-year to £3.95 billion during January–March 2026, while textile fabric imports also edged lower, according to Office for National Statistics data.
March clothing imports fell 6.34 per cent from a year earlier.
The figures reflected softer apparel demand after the UK recorded moderate import growth in 2025 following a sharp decline in 2023.

title: Japan’s Asics posts record Q1 earnings on broad regional growth
summary:
Japanese sportswear company Asics Corporation has reported record Q1 FY26 earnings, with net sales rising 29.7 per cent YoY to ¥270.2 billion (~$1.7 billion), driven by growth across categories and regions. 
Operating profit grew 36.5 per cent, while SportStyle, Onitsuka Tiger, Europe, Japan, and Southeast and South Asia led gains. 
Asics maintained its FY26 sales forecast at ¥950 billion (~$5.99 billion).

title: Canada Goose eyes FY27 growth on pricing, product depth
summary:
Canada Goose expects low-single-digit revenue growth in FY27, with adjusted EBIT margin at 11 per cent to 12 per cent. 
In Q4 FY26, revenue rose 18 per cent to CA$453.3 million (~$330.91 million), supported by DTC and wholesale growth. 
Full-year revenue increased 13.3 per cent to CA$1.53 billion (~$1.12 billion), though operating income declined amid higher SG&A expenses.

title: Vietnam’s flat apparel exports hide the real trade signal
summary:
Vietnam’s textile and apparel sector showed modest export growth in early 2026, but stronger fabric imports, rising FDI and growing US market share signalled deeper sourcing confidence. 
While overall US apparel imports declined, Vietnam continued gaining relevance as global buyers used it as a hedge against tariff uncertainty, supply-chain risk and China’s weakening position in the US market.

title: US' Wolverine Worldwide Q1 EPS rises 60% on brand momentum
summary:
Wolverine Worldwide’s Q1 FY26 revenue rose 11 per cent YoY to $457.6 million, led by strong growth at Merrell and Saucony. 
Gross margin stayed flat at 47.6 per cent, while operating margin improved to 7.4 per cent. 
Net earnings increased to $20.2 million, and diluted EPS rose to $0.24. 
The company maintained its FY26 revenue outlook of $1.96-1.98 billion.

title: India’s Pearl Global’s FY26 revenue crosses $521 mn milestone
summary:
Pearl Global Industries has reported its highest-ever FY26 revenue of ₹5,025 crore (~$523.93 million), up 11.5 per cent YoY, driven by volume growth and value-added products. 
PAT rose 17 per cent to ₹270 crore (~$28.15 million), while Q4 revenue hit ₹1,314 crore (~$137 million). 
The company shipped 78.1 million pieces. 
Its net worth stands at ₹1,438 crore (~$149.93 million).

title: Bangladesh apparel reset: Compliance edge or energy trap?
summary:
Bangladesh is shifting its apparel pitch from low-cost production to verifiable, traceable and compliant sourcing. 
BGMEA’s AWARE, Open Supply Hub and GIZ deals strengthen DPP readiness, but energy shortages and weak ten-month exports remain major risks. 
US tariff relief helps, yet fibre-origin rules and policy uncertainty complicate sourcing decisions.

title: UGG boots that last 15 years: Inside Deckers’ strategy
summary:
Deckers is positioning durability as central to UGG’s sustainability and circularity strategy, with long-lasting products, repairability and emotional consumer attachment driving value.
However, EVA recycling, product disassembly and post-consumer infrastructure remain key challenges.
UGG Renew, LWG Gold-rated tanneries and comfort-led innovation support the brand’s circular footwear approach.
